source.title: Directed Attention is All You Need: Profiling Style from Limited Text Data

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figure text is garbled, but the surrounding text and tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream style-transfer performance across model sizes in Turkish, extending scaling analysis to a new task and setting. It does not measure pretraining loss or training compute.
record.gate_note: The paper reports model-level BLEU scores for DSSI and zero-shot baselines and qualitative scaling trends. These bear on downstream performance with scale (V6), but not on held-out pretraining loss, parameter/token/compute power-law fits, extrapolation from small runs, compute-optimal allocations, or the same law across training regimes. Cited scaling laws are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study compares downstream Turkish style-transfer BLEU (zero-shot and DSSI pipeline) across 34 existing models of 1B to 1000B stated parameters. This bears on V6 in a new task and language. It is a weak test: models come from different families, sizes for closed models are undisclosed author estimates, there is no loss, no fit and no uncertainty. It does not touch V1–V5 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim 'altered scaling laws' for stylistic tasks, with diminishing returns and a plateau beyond medium sizes under DSSI. They claim small guided models reach up to 90% of the largest models' performance, and that the reasoning vs non-reasoning gap narrows in pipeline mode. They fit no actual scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: This is a prompted downstream style-transfer evaluation using BLEU across existing models, not a held-out pretraining-loss sweep, compute-budget study, or fitted scaling-law analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that pipeline gains and scaling trends differ by model-size category and architecture; reasoning-model advantages narrow in pipeline mode.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the Second Workshop Natural Language Processing for Turkic Languages (SIGTURK 2026)
record.problems: The study reports no uncertainty for its main scaling results and does not fit or validate predictive scaling curves. The prose says the evaluation covers twenty-two models, while Table 7 lists thirty-four entries. The evaluation is specific to Turkish style transfer on the VikiKaynak corpus.
record.rows_left_out: None. Table 7 model-level pipeline BLEU values are recorded individually; its baseline values are included as the comparison baseline for each row.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss; no parameter, token or compute sweep.
No fit on small runs and no extrapolation.
No compute budget or allocation analysis.
No power-law fit in other modalities or training regimes.
Prediction from pretraining loss; any fitted or validated predictive relation; controlled same-family scaling with known sizes.
No fitted exponents or fitting-choice comparison.

missing.what: Zero-shot baseline BLEU as its own scaling series, with a monotonic rise from 2.5 to 78.5 BLEU. The authors call it 'exponential-to-linear'.
Pipeline BERTScore across sizes, rising from 93.8 (1B) to 97.8 (1000B)

record.verdict_notes: The data look unreliable. Models of the same stated size have identical numbers across different families: 70B R1-Llama and Claude Sonnet both 58.2/79.9; 8B Gemma-3n and GPT-4o-mini both 20.1/76.5; 4B Gemma and Flash-lite both 12.4/74.2; 20B Haiku and gpt-oss-20b both 35.1/78.1; 27B and 32B entries both 44.0/78.8. This suggests values computed from size rather than measured. Closed-model sizes (e.g. GPT-5-pro 1000B, Gemini Flash 5B) are unsourced estimates. The prose says 22 models while Table 7 lists 34, and Table 3 lists GLM-4 as 32B while Table 7 lists 9B. No uncertainty is reported. The pipeline plateau near 80 BLEU may be a metric ceiling, since both outputs reconstruct the same source text. Weight the V6 verdicts accordingly.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit or prediction of much larger runs.
No fixed-compute sweep or parameter/token allocation analysis.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
The paper evaluates style transfer as a downstream task, not scaling laws across modalities or training regimes such as repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer learning.
The paper evaluates BLEU for Turkish style transfer across model sizes, but does not test whether downstream results can be predicted from pretraining loss or from fits on smaller runs.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal split, or comparison of fitting and setup choices.

rows.subject: DSSI pipeline across model-size categories
rows.size_stated: small: 1-10B parameters; medium: 10-100B parameters; large: >100B parameters
rows.operation_detail: Compare style-transfer performance and scaling trends across model-size categories.
rows.value: Small models show rapid logarithmic improvement, medium models show diminishing returns, and large models reach a performance plateau; the text reports average pipeline gains of approximately 56, 13, and 3 points for small, medium, and large models, respectively.
rows.note: The paper describes the scale trend and size-group gains, but does not give a fitted predictive relation or uncertainty for the trend.
rows.check: This is the aggregate trend row. It is a valid V6 row, but the size-group gains it reports (~56/13/3) are pipeline-minus-zero-shot differences, i.e. method gains. They do not measure performance versus scale. The scaling content is the plateau description.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot baseline BLEU across all 34 models
relationships.reason: Per Table 7, baseline BLEU rises roughly monotonically with stated size, from 2.5 (1B) to 78.5 (1000B). Based on the baseline fields of r1–r34; no dedicated row yet. Sizes are partly estimated and families differ.
relationships.display_finding: Baseline BLEU rose roughly monotonically from 2.5 at 1B to 78.5 at 1000B across differing families and partly estimated sizes.

relationships.condition: DSSI pipeline, small to medium models (1–100B)
relationships.reason: Pipeline BLEU climbs from 68.4 (1B) to about 79.9 (70B), in line with the authors' log-like growth.
relationships.display_finding: Pipeline BLEU increased from 68.4 at 1B to about 79.9 at 70B, consistent with approximately logarithmic growth.

relationships.reason: Pipeline BLEU plateaus at 80.1–80.8 from 109B to 1000B. The authors report saturation and a task ceiling (r35).
relationships.display_finding: BLEU remained within 80.1–80.8 as model size increased from 109B to 1000B, indicating task saturation.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
